citations.description: search_files for 'assertion inventory', 'parity table', 'ported 1:1', 'retired' in scripts/probe_rebar.py all returned no matches.
Ticket scope states: 'Assertion inventory table in the change description (commit message).' — the table lives in a Gerrit commit message, not a repo file.

findings.criterion: Assertion-parity table: every shell assertion mapped to ported/retired-with-reason.
findings.detail: The ticket scope specifies the assertion inventory table should appear in the commit message (Gerrit change description). No such table exists in any repository file — not in scripts/probe_rebar.py, not in docs/, not in CHANGELOG.md, and not in any other file reachable by the file tools. The criterion is untagged (codebase-verifiable), so the ticket comment attestation ('all 140 shell assertions ported 1:1 by label, 0 retired') is not sufficient evidence. The table is not verifiable from the repository.

citations.description: Shell file still exists as a transitional exec shim, not deleted.

Ticket comment: 'FIX (patchset 2/3): restore scripts/probe-rebar.sh as a 7-line transitional exec shim delegating to probe_rebar.py; created d772-6007-5d04-4101 (discovered_from) to delete the shim once this change lands.'

findings.criterion: Side-by-side run shows identical verdicts; shell deleted in the same change with ALL enumerated consumers (workflows, anti-rot test, docs) re-pointed to the Python entry point.
findings.detail: scripts/probe-rebar.sh is NOT deleted — it exists as a 7-line transitional exec shim that delegates to probe_rebar.py. The criterion explicitly requires the shell to be 'deleted in the same change.' The ticket comment explains this deviation (Gerrit executes-from-main constraint) and defers deletion to a follow-up ticket (d772-6007-5d04-4101), but the stated criterion is not met. All consumers are re-pointed (test.yml:128, gerrit-verify.yaml:209, external-integration.yml:55, test_probe_wired_into_ci.py, docs/releasing.md), but the shell deletion sub-requirement is unmet.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
